results.summary_before: This is a controller for an 8-sensor line-following robot car. It reads digital signals from an IR sensor array, computes a tracking error using a weighted method, and generates PWM signals for two DC motors to correct the trajectory. Four configuration pins allow tuning of the correction magnitude for more aggressive or smoother turns. The design requires external hardware including an 8-channel IR sensor array, analog comparators, dual DC motors, an H-bridge driver, and configuration switches.

results.summary_before: BIST-8 implements a built-in self-test architecture for an 8-bit carry-lookahead adder, including a 12-bit LFSR pattern generator, a 16-bit MISR response compactor, fault injection, and a 4-state FSM controller. In normal mode it acts as a standard adder; in BIST mode it runs 4095 test vectors and compares the MISR signature against a golden value of 0xCF77. A fault injection input forces a stuck-at-0 fault on bit 3 of the adder output, producing a faulty signature of 0x927F to demonstrate detection. The design is notable for its complete self-test capability and clear documentation of expected signatures.

results.summary_before: This design simulates a universal one-qubit quantum computer, executing operations such as reset, X/Y/Z/H/S/T gates, and measurement. Amplitudes are stored as 8-bit fixed-point numbers, and an LFSR provides pseudorandom numbers for measurement. The operation is selected via three input pins, and a start signal triggers execution; measurement results appear on an output pin, and a done signal indicates completion. The design is notable for bringing quantum computing concepts to a tiny digital chip, though it is limited to a single qubit.

results.summary_before: BioPulse Tile processes an 8-bit radar or biosignal sample stream to detect breathing cycles, classify breathing patterns (normal, fast, slow, irregular, apnea), and detect heartbeats, all using digital logic without a CPU. It includes a demo mode with synthetic patterns, and streams metrics over UART. The design is tested with a cocotb testbench and can be used with external radar or biosignal front-ends. It is notable for its comprehensive vital-sign monitoring capabilities in a tiny digital tile.

results.summary_before: This design implements an 8-bit full-duplex SPI communication system with both master and slave controllers. The master accepts 8-bit parallel data and, when started, shifts it out via MOSI while generating SCLK and CS signals, with a DONE signal indicating completion. The slave receives the data and outputs it on SLAVE_RX0, while the master's received data appears on MASTER_RX0. Testing involves applying reset, loading data, asserting START, and observing the SPI signals and received data.
results.summary: This design implements an 8-bit SPI master controller using Verilog. The master accepts 8-bit parallel data and, when started, shifts it out via MOSI while generating SCLK and CS signals, with a DONE signal indicating completion. The design includes a finite state machine with IDLE, LOAD, TRANSFER, and DONE states, and a shift register for serial transmission. Testing involves applying reset, loading data, asserting START, and observing the SPI signals.

results.notes: Removed unsupported 'industry-grade' claim from summary; source describes a standard SPI slave.
results.summary_before: This design implements an industry-grade SPI slave peripheral with an internal 8-byte register file, targeting the GlobalFoundries 180nm platform. It uses a synchronous FSM to decode SPI transactions on SCLK, MOSI, and CS_N, supporting read and write commands with a 1-byte command phase followed by a 1-byte data phase. Register 0's content is continuously driven to the output pins for real-time monitoring. Testing involves sending SPI commands to write data and verifying the output pins update accordingly.
results.summary: This design implements a standard 4-wire SPI slave peripheral with an internal 8-byte register file, targeting the GlobalFoundries 180nm platform. It uses a synchronous FSM to decode SPI transactions on SCLK, MOSI, and CS_N, supporting read and write commands with a 1-byte command phase followed by a 1-byte data phase. Register 0's content is continuously driven to the output pins for real-time monitoring. Testing involves sending SPI commands to write data and verifying the output pins update accordingly.
